A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Learning the Minimum Action Distance. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and rescaled results.

before.justification: V2 reports original distance-learning experiments, hyperparameter ablations, and downstream planning success rates in Section 7 and Appendices E–H.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds AntMaze distance-learning and planning results, plus a qualitative MediumMaze analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed quasimetric, losses, and target-network updates remain unchanged. Tables 2–3 revise the reported network configuration from (512, 512, 256, 128) to (512, 512, 256). Appendix H also introduces an AntMaze planning adaptation that retrieves Navigate trajectory segments using the learned distance.

E1.justification: V3 adds OGBench AntMaze Medium Navigate, Stitch, and Explore distance-learning evaluations, plus Medium Explore planning. This extends coverage from grid worlds and ball navigation to torque-controlled quadruped locomotion with 29-dimensional observations and eight-dimensional actions. Existing environments remain covered.

E2.justification: QRL and Hilbert remain the evaluated external baselines in the distance-learning and planning comparisons. The new AntMaze experiments extend this same comparator set. Wide Norm and IQE remain in the quasimetric ablations; the added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported training settings change substantially: Table 4 changes QRL's batch size from 256 to 1024, and Tables 2–3 change Adam to AdamW and revise network dimensions. Section 7 changes the stated budget from 50,000 to 50,000/100,000 steps, although v2 already plots 100,000-step maze experiments. Appendix H adds the distinct AntMaze trajectory-retrieval protocol. These reported revisions do not establish reruns; the optimizer prose still says Adam.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.1 and Figure 8 provide a MediumMaze case study visualizing learned distances around walls and across different goals. The existing latent-dimension, quasimetric-choice, and dataset-size ablations retain their evidence; their display changes are not new analyses.

E5.justification: Section 7 changes its stated run count from five to three, while corresponding full-results captions change from three seeds in v2 Figures 8–9 to five in v3 Figures 9–10. Figure 3 still states three seeds, and ablations retain five. Min/max bands and planning standard deviations remain. Reporting changes are definite, but actual run counts remain inconsistent.

E6.justification: V3 adds distance-learning results for three AntMaze scenarios and an AntMaze Medium Explore planning row: MadDist 0.80 ± 0.21, QRL 0.49 ± 0.23, TDMadDist 0.39 ± 0.25, and Hilbert 0.01 ± 0.07. These substantially extend the reported empirical outcomes. The six PointMaze planning rows are unchanged, and retained benchmark curves match after accounting for changed axis scaling.

T1.justification: Section 5 removes the explicit Wide Norm and IQE mathematical constructions, including the interval-union and aggregation definitions, without relocating them. The MAD definition, uniqueness theorem, ReLU propositions, proofs, and loss derivations remain unchanged. Appendix C.1 adds intuitive explanation rather than new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and three central contributions remain substantively unchanged. The introduction adds broader assertions that the learning approach is inherently robust to stochasticity, agnostic to the collection policy, and trainable on datasets of any quality, including random, expert, and fragmented trajectories.

C2.justification: The discussion newly attributes TDMadDist's advantage over Hilbert to its distance parametrization and learning objective, including in symmetric environments. Appendix F interprets the new heatmaps as capturing maze geometry. Appendix H explains that random AntMaze actions rarely produce coordinated locomotion, motivating trajectory-based proposals.

D1.justification: V3 adds AntMaze state/action specifications, dataset descriptions, and the grid-based MAD approximation. Appendix H documents trajectory retrieval and specifies discretized PointMaze action sampling. Hyperparameter tables are revised, and Appendix D adds a promise to release code upon acceptance; it does not establish current code availability.

R1.justification: Related work adds Agarwal et al. and a paragraph positioning MAD against Laplacian representations, citing Wu, Machado, and two Wang works. AdamW references are also added. These extend the existing positioning without replacing its central comparison with symmetric distances and prior quasimetric learning.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted additions and rewrites in the introduction, related work, and discussion, shortens Section 5, and adds explanatory bullets in Appendix C. Appendix F is divided into qualitative and quantitative subsections. The overall section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially revised: correlation plots use nonlinear vertical scaling, Figure 3 replaces its KeyDoor panels with AntMaze, and new Figures 8 and 11 add heatmaps and AntMaze results. Figure 2 changes environment images, Table 1 is expanded and moved, and ablation colors, uncertainty-band outlines, and legends are adjusted. Retained curves are largely redisplayed evidence.

improvement.justification: AntMaze adds validation in a demanding locomotion setting absent from v2, while the MediumMaze visualization and expanded related work improve interpretation and context. These provide a limited overall quality gain. Conflicting seed and optimizer descriptions weaken reproducibility, and the AntMaze Explore planning result requires Navigate trajectories, limiting how broadly that new evidence can be interpreted.
